attribution_limitations: Source conflict on the digoxin interpretation: the case text calls the plasma analysis positive for poisoning with digoxin (4.8 ng/mL), but the same paragraph says the plasma digoxin levels were low (so specific antibodies were not prescribed) and the discussion says the concentrations did not reach toxic levels. The 4.8 ng/mL value itself is undisputed; the flag and the digoxin poisoning diagnosis are review_only.

The abstract lists acetaminophen and opiates in the combined intoxication, while the case text reports acetaminophen, opioids and barbiturates within normal ranges and ingestion of acetaminophen/tramadol without a measured amount.

Toxicology plasma was harvested at ~1 h following ingestion, whereas Table 1 is headed as results upon presentation and ingestion was ~30 min before arrival. The text cites Table 1 for this analysis; the exact sampling time is not reconciled.
Source conflict on the severity grade of left ventricular dysfunction: moderate in the case text and abstract, mild in the discussion. Only the LVEF 40% value is accepted.
The abstract says Takotsubo cardiomyopathy was suspected after the angiogram, while the case text says the diagnosis was established by the Mayo Clinic and 2018 International Takotsubo criteria.
The case reports heart rate 51 bpm and 90/40 mmHg on arrival, then 65 bpm and 78/45 mmHg on physical examination; their relative timing is not stated.

Day counts use different anchors (day 3 from the time of admission, day 6 after drug poisoning, day 6 and day 8 with no anchor); the 6-month follow-up is stated only in the discussion about our subject.
Source conflict on apical wall motion for the day-3 echocardiogram: severe hypokinesis of the apical segments of the anterior and inferior wall in the case text, akinesia of the apex in the abstract.
Lactate dehydrogenase is said to be increased only inside a hedged explanation of the lactate rise; no LDH value or time is given and LDH is not in Table 1.
